approachQuestion.prompt:
A Trail for a Message

Given an h by w character grid and a nonempty word, return whether some orthogonally adjacent cell sequence spells the word. A cell may be used at most once in that sequence. Different attempts may reuse cells. Do not modify the supplied grid.

Examples:
grid=["ab","dc"], word="abcd" -> true via (0,0),(0,1),(1,1),(1,0).
grid=["ab"], word="aba" -> false.

Constraints: 1 <= h,w <= 6; 1 <= L=word.length <= h*w; lowercase letters.

options.text: Try all matching starts with depth-first search. Mark a cell while it belongs to the current trail and unmark on every return, including early success. Match one new character per move.
options.feedback: Only cells in the current trail are forbidden. Restoring membership permits another branch to use a cell without permitting reuse within a single trail.

options.text: Keep one visited array marked permanently across all starting cells.
options.feedback: On grid=["ab","ac"], word="acba", a failed first start marks (0,0), which is needed at the end of the valid trail (1,0),(1,1),(0,1),(0,0). Permanent marks wrongly block it.

options.text: Search adjacent matching characters without tracking used cells.
options.feedback: On grid=["ab"], word="aba", returning to the first cell would falsely produce true.

options.text: For each candidate step, copy the whole visited array into a child-specific array rather than marking and undoing one shared array.
options.feedback: Branch-local copies are correct, but copying the entire grid state per child is removable by undoing one changed mark.

feedback.reason: Only cells in the current trail are forbidden. Restoring membership permits another branch to use a cell without permitting reuse within a single trail.
details: Allocate an h*w boolean array. Try every matching start. A call for a matched cell marks it, tests at most four neighbors against the next character and unmarked state, recurses on matches, and unmarks on return. Succeed after matching the last character.
Mark a cell only on the current path and unmark it on return. Global permanent marking would reject a later valid start using that cell; omitting path marking would reuse a cell within one trail.

“Try all matching starts with depth-first search. Mark a cell while it belongs to the current trail and unmark on every return, including early success. Match one new character per move.”: Only cells in the current trail are forbidden. Restoring membership permits another branch to use a cell without permitting reuse within a single trail.

“Keep one visited array marked permanently across all starting cells.”: On grid=["ab","ac"], word="acba", a failed first start marks (0,0), which is needed at the end of the valid trail (1,0),(1,1),(0,1),(0,0). Permanent marks wrongly block it.
“Search adjacent matching characters without tracking used cells.”: On grid=["ab"], word="aba", returning to the first cell would falsely produce true.

“For each candidate step, copy the whole visited array into a child-specific array rather than marking and undoing one shared array.”: Branch-local copies are correct, but copying the entire grid state per child is removable by undoing one changed mark.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze `acm-b18-05-search` only. Let N=h*w and V be the actual number of matched-cell calls executed before the method stops, summed over starts. Initialize N marks and scan all N starts. Each call checks at most four neighbors; no trail is returned. Choose the tightest stated time and auxiliary-space pair. Count recursion and mutable working state; exclude supplied input and returned output storage, but include copying work in time. Primitive integer/index operations and preallocated-array updates cost constant time; dynamic appends are amortized constant time. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(N + V) time, O(N + L) auxiliary space
O(N + V) time, O(L) auxiliary space
O(N·V) time, O(N + L) auxiliary space
O(N + L) time, O(N + L) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Grid initialization plus bounded neighbor work per matched-cell state determines time.
details: Initializing and scanning the grid costs N, and each matched-cell call performs bounded neighbor work. Thus total performed work is proportional to N+V.
The visited array has N entries. The stack has at most L frames. The stated sum counts both; since L<=N it is also O(N).

Let N=h*w and V be the actual number of matched-cell calls executed before the method stops, summed over starts. Initialize N marks and scan all N starts. Each call checks at most four neighbors; no trail is returned.
“O(N + V) time, O(L) auxiliary space”: This forgets the N-entry visited array on the general grid.
“O(N·V) time, O(N + L) auxiliary space”: The method does not copy or rescan the full grid in each call.
“O(N + L) time, O(N + L) auxiliary space”: Many different trails can match the same word prefixes.
